pages.title: Apple
pages.extract: An apple is the round, edible fruit of an apple tree (Malus spp.). Fruit trees of the orchard or domestic apple (Malus domestica), the most widely grown in the genus, are cultivated worldwide.

pages.title: Cat
pages.extract: The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal. It is a member of Felidae, the family of mammals in the order Carnivora also colloquially referred to as cats.

pages.title: House
pages.extract: A house is a residential building. It may range in complexity from a rudimentary hut to a complex structure of wood, masonry, concrete or other material, outfitted with plumbing, electrical, and heating, ventilation, and air conditioning systems.

pages.title: Tree
pages.description: Perennial woody plant with elongated trunk
pages.extract: In botany, a tree is a perennial plant with an elongated stem, or trunk, usually supporting branches and leaves. In some usages, the definition of a tree may be narrower, e.g., including only woody plants with secondary growth, only plants that are usable for timber, or only plants above a specified height.

pages.title: Serendipity
pages.extract: Serendipity is an unplanned fortunate discovery. The term was coined by Horace Walpole in 1754, after he read a Persian fairy tale called The Three Princes of Serendip, whose heroes constantly made lucky discoveries.

pages.title: Bob Crane
pages.extract:
Robert Edward Crane (July 13, 1928 – June 29, 1978) was an American actor, drummer, radio personality, disc jockey and star of the CBS sitcom Hogan's Heroes.
Crane was a drummer from age 11, and began his entertainment career as a radio personality, beginning in Hornell, New York, and later in Connecticut.

pages.title: Crane (machine)
pages.extract: A crane is a machine used to move materials both vertically and horizontally, utilizing a system of a boom, hoist, wire ropes or chains, and sheaves for lifting and relocating heavy objects within the swing of its boom. The device uses one or more simple machines, such as the lever and pulley, to create mechanical advantage to do its work.

pages.title: Sandhill crane
pages.extract: The sandhill crane (Antigone canadensis) is a species of large crane of North America and extreme northeastern Siberia. The common name of this bird refers to its habitat, such as the Platte River, on the edge of Nebraska's Sandhills on the American Great Plains.

pages.title: Ichabod Crane
pages.description: Fictional character from The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
pages.extract: Ichabod Crane is a fictional character and the protagonist in Washington Irving's short story "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow". Crane is portrayed in the original work, and in most adaptations, as a tall, lanky individual.

pages.title: Crane (bird)
pages.extract: Cranes are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes. The family has 15 species placed in four genera which are Antigone, Balearica, Leucogeranus, and Grus.

pages.title: Common crane
pages.description: Species of bird also known as Eurasian crane
pages.extract: The common crane (Grus grus), also known as the Eurasian crane, is a bird of the family Gruidae, the cranes. A medium-sized species, it is the only crane commonly found in Europe besides the demoiselle crane (Grus virgo) and the Siberian crane (Leucogeranus leucogeranus) that only are regular in the far eastern part of the continent.

pages.title: Siberian crane
pages.extract: The Siberian crane (Leucogeranus leucogeranus), also known as the Siberian white crane or the snow crane, is a bird of the family Gruidae, the cranes. They are distinctive among the cranes: adults are nearly all snowy white, except for their black primary feathers that are visible in flight, and with two breeding populations in the Arctic tundra of western and eastern Russia.

pages.title: Demoiselle crane
pages.extract: The demoiselle crane (Grus virgo) is a species of crane found in central Eurosiberia, ranging from the Black Sea to Mongolia and Northeast China. There is also a small breeding population in Turkey.

pages.title: Antigone (bird)
pages.extract: Antigone is a genus of large birds in the crane family. The species in this genus were formerly placed in the genus Grus.

pages.title: Great blue heron
pages.extract: The great blue heron (Ardea herodias) is a large wading bird in the heron family (Ardeidae), common near shores of open water and wetlands over most of North and Central America, as well as Northwestern South America, the Caribbean, and the Galápagos Islands. It is occasionally found in the Azores and is a rare vagrant to Europe.

pages.title: Grey heron
pages.extract: The grey heron (Ardea cinerea) is a long-legged wading bird of the heron family, Ardeidae, native throughout  Europe, Asia, and most of Africa. It is resident in much of its range, but some populations from the more northern parts migrate southwards in autumn.

pages.title: Great egret
pages.extract: The great egret (Ardea alba), also known as the common egret, large egret, great white egret, or great white heron, is a large, widely distributed egret.  The four subspecies occur in Asia, Africa, the Americas, and southern Europe.

pages.title: Ardea (bird)
pages.extract: Ardea is a genus of herons. These herons are generally large in size, typically 80–100 cm or more in length.

pages.title: List of official city birds
pages.extract: The following is an incomplete list of official city birds, organized by country.

pages.title: Crane (machine)
pages.extract: A crane is a machine used to move materials both vertically and horizontally, utilizing a system of a boom, hoist, wire ropes or chains, and sheaves for lifting and relocating heavy objects within the swing of its boom. The device uses one or more simple machines, such as the lever and pulley, to create mechanical advantage to do its work.

pages.title: Claw machine
pages.extract: A claw machine is a type of arcade game. Modern claw machines are upright cabinets with glass boxes that are lit from the inside and have a joystick-controlled claw at the top, which is coin-operated and positioned over a pile of prizes, dropped into the pile, and picked up to unload the prize or lack thereof into a chute.

pages.title: Gantry crane
pages.description: Type of overhead crane used in industrial environments
pages.extract: A gantry crane is a crane built atop a gantry, which is a structure used to straddle an object or workspace. They can range from enormous "full" gantry cranes, capable of lifting some of the heaviest loads in the world, to small shop cranes, used for tasks such as lifting automobile engines out of vehicles.

pages.title: Lifting hook
pages.description: Device for lifting loads with a hoist or crane
pages.extract: A lifting hook is a device for grabbing and lifting loads by means of a device such as a hoist or crane. A lifting hook is usually equipped with a safety latch to prevent the disengagement of the lifting wire rope sling, chain or rope to which the load is attached.

pages.title: Treadwheel crane
pages.description: Wooden, human powered, hoisting and lowering device
pages.extract: A treadwheel crane (Latin: magna rota) is a wooden, human-powered hoisting and lowering device. It was primarily used during the Roman period and the Middle Ages in the building of castles and cathedrals.

pages.title: Theo de Raadt
pages.extract: Theo de Raadt ( də RAWT, Dutch: [ˈteːjoː də ˈraːt]; born 19 May 1968) is a South African-born software engineer who lives in Calgary, Canada.

pages.title: Bane (band)
pages.extract: Bane is an American hardcore punk band that began in 1995 as a side project between Aaron Dalbec (then of Converge) and Damon Bellorado. Dalbec approached Matt Firestone to sing and they played under the moniker of Gateway for a few shows, before Firestone parted ways to focus on other projects.

pages.title: Crotalum
pages.description: Kind of clapper used in religious dances in classical antiquity
pages.extract:
In classical antiquity, a crotalum, (κρόταλον krotalon) plural crotala, was a kind of clapper or castanet used in religious dances by groups in ancient Greece and elsewhere, including the Korybantes.
The term has been erroneously supposed by some writers to be the same as the sistrum.

pages.title: Forked River Nuclear Power Plant
pages.description: Proposed nuclear power plant in New Jersey
pages.extract: The Forked River Nuclear Power Plant was a proposed nuclear power plant in Lacey Township in Ocean County, New Jersey.  It was proposed as a single 1,070 MW reactor in 1969 to be built by Combustion Engineering and operated by Jersey Central Power and Light.

pages.title: Ptilozamites
pages.extract: Ptilozamites is an extinct genus of pteridosperm (colloquially known as "seed ferns"), known from the Triassic and Early Jurassic of the Northern Hemisphere. It is associated with the pollen organ Harrisiothecium.

pages.title: Crane (bird)
pages.extract: Cranes are a type of large bird with long legs and necks in the biological family Gruidae of the order Gruiformes. The family has 15 species placed in four genera which are Antigone, Balearica, Leucogeranus, and Grus.

pages.title: Red-crowned crane
pages.description: Species of large bird from East Asia
pages.extract: The red-crowned crane (Grus japonensis), also called the Japanese crane and the Manchurian crane, is a large Northeast Asian crane among the rarest cranes in the world. In some parts of its range, it is known as a symbol of luck, longevity, and fidelity.

pages.title: Ichabod Crane
pages.description: Fictional character from The Legend of Sleepy Hollow
pages.extract: Ichabod Crane is a fictional character and the protagonist in Washington Irving's short story "The Legend of Sleepy Hollow". Crane is portrayed in the original work, and in most adaptations, as a tall, lanky individual.

pages.title: Black-necked crane
pages.description: Species of large bird from Asia
pages.extract: The black-necked crane (Grus nigricollis) is a medium-sized crane in Asia that breeds on the Tibetan Plateau and remote parts of India and Bhutan. It is 139 cm (55 in) long with a 235 cm (7.71 ft) wingspan, and it weighs 5.5 kg (12 lb).

pages.title: List of cranes
pages.extract: Cranes are tall wading birds in the family Gruidae. Cranes are found on every continent except for South America and Antarctica and inhabit a variety of open habitats, although most species prefer to live near water.

pages.title: Cat
pages.extract: The cat (Felis catus), also called domestic cat and house cat, is a small domesticated carnivorous mammal. It is a member of Felidae, the family of mammals in the order Carnivora also colloquially referred to as cats.

pages.title: Cat (disambiguation)
pages.description: Topics referred to by the same term
pages.extract: The cat (Felis catus) is a domesticated feline species.

pages.title: Black Cat
pages.description: Topics referred to by the same term

pages.title: .cat
pages.description: Internet top-level domain for the Catalan people
pages.extract: .cat (spelled out in Catalan: punt cat [ˈpuŋ ˈkat]) is a sponsored top-level domain intended to be used to highlight the Catalan language, developed by ICANN and Fundació puntCAT (now known as Accent Obert).

pages.title: Doja Cat
pages.extract: Amala Ratna Zandile Dlamini (born October 21, 1995), known professionally as Doja Cat ( DOH-jə), is an American rapper and singer-songwriter. Regarded as the "Queen of Pop-Rap", she is known for her musical versatility, live performance skills and humorous internet presence.
